newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wiener Staedtische says H1 premium income down.
newsitem.headline: Wiener Staedtische says H1 premium income down.

text.p: Austrian insurer Wiener Staedtische said on Tuesday its premium income in the first half fell 11.9 percent to 9.13 billion schillings.
In a statement, Wiener Staedtische said insurance payments over the same period slipped 0.4 percent to 5.19 billion schillings.
Wiener Staedtische said one-off premium payments had fallen by almost two-thirds to 660 million schillings after the scrapping of tax relief against lump sum payments into life insurance policies.
In contrast, regular life insurance policy payments had risen slightly. Overall, life insurance premium income dropped 30 percent to 2.72 billion schillings in the first half.
"But because there was a boom in one-off investments from January to May last year (before the law change), we expect the decline over the full year to be smaller," Wiener Staedtische said.

Premium income from accident insurance rose 1.9 percent to 4.76 billion schillings. Health insurance premium income eased just 1.8 percent to 1.65 billion schillings despite an eight percent drop in prices. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
